strategy_title: Larger XBLOCK for Broadcast Alignment Caused Regression
strategy_description: Increasing XBLOCK to align tile boundaries with a broadcast dimension (1024 elements) improved scheduler eligibility (No Eligible dropped from 73% to 9%) and occupancy (32% to 79%), but the kernel still regressed by 46% in wall time (42.6us to 62.1us). The root cause of the regression is that the autotune decorator selected a larger block size (256 threads) which increased register pressure from 16 to 24 registers/thread, and the total executed instruction count exploded from 8.4M to 43M — a 5x increase — indicating the wider tile caused significantly more redundant or predicated work (Avg. Not Predicated Off Threads Per Warp dropped to 27.96 from 32.0). Despite better scheduler utilization, the 5x instruction count increase dominated and caused the slowdown.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=128, grid=(65536,), 16 regs/thread, 8.4M instructions
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]
    x0 = xindex % 1024
    x1 = xindex // 1024
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0, None)
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + x1, None)
    tl.store(out_ptr0 + xindex, tmp0 + tmp1, None)

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)
kernel[grid](..., XBLOCK=128)

@triton.autotune(
    configs=[Config({'XBLOCK': 2048}, num_warps=8), Config({'XBLOCK': 1024}, num_warps=8), ...],
    key=['xnumel'],
)
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    xmask = xindex < xnumel  # <-- now uses dynamic mask (unnecessary for aligned sizes)
    x0 = xindex % 1024
    x1 = xindex // 1024
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0, xmask)  # masked load adds overhead
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + x1, xmask)
    tl.store(out_ptr0 + xindex, tmp0 + tmp1, xmask)

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # grid NOT updated to use meta['XBLOCK']
kernel[grid](...)  # autotune config ignored because grid is hardcoded!
applicable_when: Kernel has low scheduler eligibility (<30% eligible warps), high L1TEX stall cycles (>70% of warp cycles), and tile size is misaligned with a broadcast dimension causing redundant memory loads.
do_not_apply_when: The grid lambda is not updated to use meta['XBLOCK'] — if the grid remains hardcoded to the old block size, autotune will select configs but the grid will be wrong, causing 2x more threads than elements and a 5x instruction count explosion. Also avoid introducing dynamic xmask (xindex < xnumel) when xnumel is exactly divisible by all candidate XBLOCK values, as this adds unnecessary predication overhead and reduces Not Predicated Off Threads Per Warp.
framework_notes: Critical Triton autotune implementation flaw: when adding @triton.autotune, the grid in the kernel launch site MUST be updated to a lambda using meta['XBLOCK']. In this case the grid remained hardcoded as (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),) while autotune selected larger blocks, causing the grid to launch 2x more thread blocks than needed for XBLOCK=256. Additionally, changing xmask from tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1) to xindex < xnumel introduced unnecessary predication for sizes that are exactly divisible by all candidate XBLOCKs.

strategy_title: Persistent Kernel with Wrong Grid Causes Severe Regression
strategy_description: Replacing a flat grid with a persistent kernel (while-loop over tiles) caused a 5.7x slowdown (42.8us → 244.6us) because the grid was never updated from (cdiv(xnumel, 128),) = 65536 CTAs to the intended 132 CTAs. The persistent kernel body ran inside 65536 CTAs each iterating the while loop, causing L2 traffic to explode (L2 Compression Input Sectors: 1M → 30.7M, L2 Cache Throughput: 17% → 84%) and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction to skyrocket from 6.6 to 138.8 cycles due to LG queue full stalls (50.6% of warp cycles). Despite occupancy improving from 20.6% to 90.4%, the massive increase in memory traffic and instruction count (14M → 18.8M) made the kernel far slower — the persistent loop ran ~62 iterations per CTA across all 65536 CTAs instead of only 132.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: flat grid, 65536 CTAs, 128 threads each, 16 regs/thread
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    xmask = xindex < xnumel
    x0 = xindex % 1024
    x1 = xindex // 1024
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0, xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + x1, xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
    tl.store(out_ptr0 + xindex, tmp0 + tmp1, xmask)

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # = 65536
kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, arg_2, 8388608, XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (intended): persistent grid of 132 CTAs, while loop over 8192 tiles
# ACTUAL (buggy): grid still = 65536, while loop runs 62 iterations per CTA
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    TILE_SIZE: tl.constexpr = 1024
    NUM_SMS: tl.constexpr = 132
    total_tiles = 8192
    sm_id = tl.program_id(0)  # 0..65535 (NOT 0..131 as intended!)
    col_idx = tl.arange(0, TILE_SIZE)
    row_vals = tl.load(in_ptr0 + col_idx)  # 1024 floats loaded per CTA
    tile_id = sm_id
    while tile_id < total_tiles:  # most CTAs: sm_id >= 8192, loop never executes
        col_val = tl.load(in_ptr1 + tile_id)
        result = row_vals + col_val
        tl.store(out_ptr0 + tile_id * TILE_SIZE + col_idx, result)
        tile_id += NUM_SMS  # stride=132, but grid=65536

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # BUG: still 65536, not 132!
kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, arg_2, 8388608, XBLOCK=128)
applicable_when: Never — this is a pure implementation flaw. The persistent kernel concept is sound but the grid was not updated.
do_not_apply_when: Always verify the grid launch site is updated to match the persistent kernel's intended CTA count. When converting a flat kernel to a persistent kernel, the grid MUST change from (cdiv(N, BLOCK),) to (NUM_SMS,). Failing to update the grid causes all CTAs with program_id >= total_tiles to load in_ptr0 (TILE_SIZE floats) wastefully and then immediately exit the while loop, while CTAs with program_id < total_tiles each process only a single tile instead of ~62 — the opposite of the intended behavior. The register pressure increase (16 → 28 regs/thread) from holding TILE_SIZE=1024 elements in registers also reduces Block Limit Registers from 32 to 16, which can cap occupancy in other contexts.
framework_notes: Critical Triton persistent kernel implementation flaw: the grid at the call site MUST be updated from (cdiv(xnumel, BLOCK),) to (NUM_SMS,) when converting to a persistent while-loop kernel. In this case the grid remained (65536,) while the kernel body used NUM_SMS=132 as the stride, causing 65536 CTAs to each load TILE_SIZE=1024 floats from in_ptr0 (65536x more loads than intended), and only CTAs 0..8191 performed any useful work. The L2 traffic explosion (30x more sectors) and LG queue full stalls (138.8 cycles/instruction vs 6.6) are the direct profiling signatures of this bug.

strategy_title: Persistent While-Loop Kernel with Unchanged Grid: 46x Regression
strategy_description: Adding a persistent while-loop (tile_id += NUM_SMS=132) to a flat elementwise kernel while leaving the launch grid hardcoded at (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK),) = 65536 CTAs caused a catastrophic ~46x wall-time regression (42.6us → 1960us). The executed instruction count exploded from 6.8M to 1.18B (173x) because all 65536 CTAs entered the while-loop and each processed multiple tiles, instead of only the intended 132 CTAs. Despite occupancy improving from 32.5% to 99.4% and scheduler eligibility improving (No Eligible: 78% → 24%), the instruction explosion completely dominated. The persistent kernel pattern is only correct when the grid is simultaneously changed to (NUM_SMS,).
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: flat grid, 65536 CTAs, 6.8M instructions, 42.6us
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)
    x0 = xindex % 1024
    x1 = xindex // 1024
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0)
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + x1)
    tl.store(out_ptr0 + xindex, tmp0 + tmp1)

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # = 65536
kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, arg_2, 8388608, XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (BROKEN): persistent while-loop body, grid still 65536 CTAs!
# Each of 65536 CTAs runs the full while-loop → 173x instruction explosion
@triton.autotune(configs=[...], key=['xnumel'])
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, in_ptr1, out_ptr0, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    NUM_SMS: tl.constexpr = 132
    num_tiles = tl.cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK)  # 8192
    sm_id = tl.program_id(0)  # 0..65535 (NOT 0..131 as intended!)
    tile_id = sm_id
    while tile_id < num_tiles:  # CTAs 0..8191 each run ~62 iterations!
        xoffset = tile_id * XBLOCK
        xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)
        x0 = xindex % 1024
        x1 = xindex // 1024
        tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
        tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + x1, eviction_policy='evict_last')
        tl.store(out_ptr0 + xindex, tmp0 + tmp1, eviction_policy='evict_first')
        tile_id += NUM_SMS  # stride=132, but grid=65536 → WRONG

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # BUG: still 65536, must be (NUM_SMS,) = 132
kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, arg_2, 8388608)  # 1.18B instructions, 1960us
applicable_when: Never apply this pattern without simultaneously updating the grid. The persistent kernel concept is valid for kernels with low occupancy and high CTA dispatch overhead, but ONLY when the grid is changed to (NUM_SMS,).
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply the persistent while-loop pattern if the launch site grid is not simultaneously changed from (cdiv(N, BLOCK),) to (NUM_SMS,). If the grid remains the original large value while the kernel body uses tile_id += NUM_SMS, CTAs with program_id in [0, num_tiles) will each redundantly process all tiles assigned to their stride group, causing an instruction count explosion proportional to (original_grid_size / NUM_SMS). The profiling signature is: executed instructions >> expected, occupancy near 100%, ALU pipeline over-utilized (>90%), duration >> baseline. Also note that adding @triton.autotune while keeping the grid hardcoded (not a lambda using meta['XBLOCK']) compounds the bug.
framework_notes: This is the FOURTH consecutive iteration with the same grid/body mismatch bug in Triton persistent kernels. The kernel body was correctly rewritten as a while-loop with tile_id += NUM_SMS=132, but the grid at the call site remained (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),) = 65536 instead of being changed to (NUM_SMS,) = 132. In Triton, the grid and kernel body must always be co-designed: persistent scheduling with stride=NUM_SMS requires grid=(NUM_SMS,) at the launch site. Additionally, @triton.autotune was added but the grid was not updated to a lambda using meta['XBLOCK'], which is a separate compounding bug.

The root cause is the same grid bug seen in iteration 2: when a persistent kernel uses a while-loop with stride=NUM_SMS, the grid MUST be set to (NUM_SMS,), not (cdiv(xnumel, BLOCK),).
